title: spec rc.6 vacated `WidgetManifest` / `WidgetSource` — the `Runtime…` prefixes may be reclaimed
body:
Recorded from the `@objectstack/spec` `17.0.0-rc.6` bump in objectstack#7100. Observation-class: nothing a user hits, no defect — an unlock that would otherwise be forgotten.

`@object-ui/types` carries `RuntimeWidgetManifest` and `RuntimeWidgetSource` under prefixes added purely to avoid colliding with spec exports of the same bare names (the objectui#3074 lesson, pinned in `packages/types/src/__tests__/page-nav-misc-spec-parity.test.ts`).

rc.6 retired the whole widget-manifest vocabulary from `@objectstack/spec/ui` — `WidgetManifest`, `WidgetSource`, `WidgetProperty`, `WidgetEvent`, `WidgetLifecycle` and their `…Schema` / `…Parsed` twins. The tripwire in that test fired exactly as designed, for the second time (objectui#3363 was the first, and reclaimed `GestureType` / `GestureConfig` on the same signal).

The reclaim is **available, not required**, so objectstack#7100's PR did not take it: both names are exported, so renaming them is a cross-package change with its own review, and that card is a `global_nav` retirement. What that PR did instead was move the two rows into the "spec no longer owns" list, so the vacancy stays pinned — if the spec ever re-publishes either name while objectui holds it, that becomes a live collision and the test goes red.

Whoever picks this up: the precedent to follow is objectui#3363's reclaim, and the reason a reclaim can be declined is written beside `PWAOfflineConfig` in the same file (there the name has a second claimant, so the prefix is still load-bearing — check that neither of these two does before renaming).
